strings.name: Ada Lovelace
strings.summary: Ada Lovelace was a British mathematical researcher who worked with Charles Babbage on the Analytical Engine. Her notes accompanying an 1843 translation set out computational procedures and imagined machines handling non-numerical subjects such as music. Often called the first programmer, she remains the subject of historical debate over the boundaries between her contributions and Babbage’s work. Her early understanding of general-purpose computing has had a lasting influence.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones. “The first programmer” is a common description; historians continue to debate the precise nature of her contributions.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Private education; studied mathematics with Mary Somerville, Augustus De Morgan and others

strings.facts.fact-03.value: Translation and notes on the Analytical Engine (1843)
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Notes on the Analytical Engine
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Published an extensively annotated translation in 1843, including steps for calculating Bernoulli numbers.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Computing beyond numbers
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Suggested that machines could manipulate symbols according to rules and might even be used to compose music.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in London
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died aged 36; her work on the Analytical Engine later became an important document in the history of computing.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes her translation and notes
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Translated Menabrea’s article and added notes discussing computational procedures and the machine’s wider uses.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Studies advanced mathematics
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Studied advanced mathematics with De Morgan, strengthening her understanding of the Analytical Engine’s mathematical principles.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Becomes Countess of Lovelace
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Her husband received an earldom, after which she became known as Ada Lovelace.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Marries William King
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Had three children after their marriage and later resumed more intensive mathematical study.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Meets Mary Somerville
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Received mathematical reading material and guidance from Somerville and took part in scientific activities.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Meets Charles Babbage
strings.timeline.event-07.text: A demonstration of the Difference Engine sparked her interest and began the relationship that led to their work on the Analytical Engine.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Born in London
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Born Augusta Ada Byron; received a private education that included mathematics.
